data.description:
## Context / Problem
`plan_review/__init__.py:709` guards signing with `verdict.get("runner") != "exempt"`, and
`docs/plan-review-gate.md` states a signature is never emitted "for an `exempt` runner
(`bug` / `session_log` tickets, which are exempt from the gate)". Neither matches behavior.

Probed on origin/main (20ae67c61) with the claim gate enabled: a `bug` ticket with a normal
plan body returns `verdict='PASS'`, **`runner='pydantic_ai'`** (NOT `'exempt'`),
`coverage.llm_ran=True`, and `signature.signed=True` with a real `head_sha`. So a bug runs a
FULL billable four-pass review and signs an attestation, rather than short-circuiting as an
exempt type.

Two things are wrong, and they may have one cause or two:
1. The exempt short-circuit does not fire for a `bug`, so exempt types pay full review cost.
2. Consequently the `runner != "exempt"` sign guard never engages, and the documented
   never-sign-for-exempt rule does not hold.

Impact is cost and contract-accuracy, not gate integrity: the claim gate exempts bugs anyway,
so a signed bug attestation grants nothing it would not already have. That is why this is
separate from melancholy-firstborn-shihtzu (`--source local`), which IS a gate-integrity hole.

Discovered while completing AC5 of epic 58f2-b6ed-363e-4608, whose "exempt results remain
unsigned" clause this invalidates. AC5 was amended to delegate the clause here.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Enable `[verify] require_plan_review_for_claim`.
2. Create a `bug` ticket with a plan body that clears the deterministic floor.
3. `rebar review-plan <id>` with an offline fake runner.
4. Observe `runner='pydantic_ai'`, `coverage.llm_ran=True`, `signature.signed=True`.

## Expected Behavior
Decide and make consistent, in one place:
- **(A)** Exempt types short-circuit as documented: `runner='exempt'`, no LLM passes run, no
  signature. Cheapest and matches the docs.
- **(B)** Exempt types are reviewable and signable by design; then remove the dead
  `runner != "exempt"` sign guard and correct `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

(A) is the recommendation — the docstring for `review_plan` already promises
"Bugs and session_logs are exempt (PASS, runner=exempt)".

## Approach
1. Trace where the exemption is supposed to short-circuit and why a `bug` bypasses it
   (is exemption keyed on ticket type, gate-enabled state, or claim-gate config?).
2. Apply (A) or (B) at the single seam that owns it.
3. Pin with a test asserting the chosen contract for `bug` and `session_log`.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py`
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reviewing a `bug` yields the chosen contract, asserted by a test: under (A),
      `runner == 'exempt'`, `coverage.llm_ran is False`, and `signature.signed is False`.
- [ ] The same holds for `session_log`.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md`'s exempt sentence matches the implemented contract.
- [ ] If (B) is chosen instead, the dead `runner != "exempt"` guard at
      `plan_review/__init__.py:709` is removed rather than left as misleading code.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default non-integration pytest suite exit zero.
data.title: Exempt ticket types are not short-circuited by plan review: a bug runs a full review and signs
